findings.description: record-job now writes two files per job (<jid>.ident then <jid>.pgid), but the completion path in both run_trial (line 1673) and run_session (line 1766) still removes only <jid>.pgid. Every finished trial/session leaves a <jid>.ident behind in .jobs/ for the life of the batch (thousands of files on a long batch). record-job itself does overwrite or remove a stale .ident on the next use of the same name, so reclaim correctness is not affected, but any consumer that globs $JOBS_DIR/* (status displays, cleanup) now sees records in a different format. Confidence: high (both rm lines visible in the diff).
findings.failure_mode: Failure: when a trial or session completes, then its .pgid is removed but its .ident persists, so .jobs/ grows by one orphan file per job and a later tool that lists .jobs/* sees `<ticks>:<sha256>` lines where it expects `<pgid> <epoch> <wds>`.
findings.suggested_fix: rm -f "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.pgid" "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.ident" at both completion sites (and in any watchdog path that already removes .pgid).
findings.failure_scenario: Failure: when a trial or session completes, then its .pgid is removed but its .ident persists, so .jobs/ grows by one orphan file per job and a later tool that lists .jobs/* sees `<ticks>:<sha256>` lines where it expects `<pgid> <epoch> <wds>`.

findings.description: Before this change the .pgid was published microseconds after `pid=$!`. Now it is published only after record-job's settle loop returns: at least ~150 ms (two reads 50 ms apart plus ~6 forks per iteration) and up to 100 iterations (≈6–8 s, longer than the 5 s the header states) when the leader never settles. During that window the job's group is in its own session (setsid) but has no .jobs/ record. record-job runs in the runner's process group, so a supervisor kill_group of the runner (hang, stop, crash-reclaim) also kills record-job before it writes, and the just-launched group is never recorded. stop_containers removes the container itself, so the practical orphan is the client-side group (timeout/docker CLI), but the invariant 'every live job has a .pgid' no longer holds. Confidence: high for the window; impact low.
findings.failure_mode: Failure: when the supervisor terminates the runner's group while record-job is still settling a freshly launched job, then that job's process group has no .pgid and is neither signalled nor listed in the reclaim groups list.
findings.suggested_fix: Accept and document the window (the header should say ≈8 s worst case, not 5 s), or write a provisional .pgid immediately and let record-job replace it atomically after the .ident lands, with reclaim treating a .pgid younger than the settle bound and without .ident as 'pending' rather than 'legacy'.
findings.failure_scenario: Failure: when the supervisor terminates the runner's group while record-job is still settling a freshly launched job, then that job's process group has no .pgid and is neither signalled nor listed in the reclaim groups list.

findings.description: The settled identity is `start_ticks:sha256(cmdline)` taken when argv[0] is not setsid/env, differs from the caller, and two reads 50 ms apart agree. reclaim then refuses to signal any group whose leader's current identity differs. Two leader shapes defeat this permanently: (a) a leader that execs again after settling — any exec-ing wrapper other than setsid/env (nice, ionice, taskset, stdbuf, flock, nohup, a shebang script that ends in `exec docker …`) whose exec takes >50 ms (cold cache of a 30–50 MB docker binary easily does) is captured pre-exec, then its cmdline changes; (b) a leader that never execs (a bash function or subshell launched with `&`), whose cmdline equals the caller's forever, so the loop times out and no .ident is written. In both cases reclaim classifies the live group as stale/legacy, removes the record and never signals it, whereas the base killed it. A third, deterministic cause: arg0 is extracted with `tr | head -n 1` under pipefail; for a cmdline larger than the pipe buffer (64 KiB) head exits first, tr gets SIGPIPE, arg0 is empty every iteration and the leader never settles. I could not see which command run-ablation.sh puts in `cmd[0]` for the `if` branch, so this is conditional on that. Confidence: medium.
findings.failure_mode: Failure: when the group leader's cmdline changes after record-job settled (or never diverges from the caller's), then on reclaim the live group is logged as stale/legacy, its record is removed and it is never TERM/KILLed, leaving the trial's client processes running after the batch is resumed.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the settle predicate structural instead of a 50 ms heuristic: record the identity only once /proc/<pgid>/exe resolves to the expected final binary (or after the leader has at least one child, since timeout/docker fork), or have run-ablation.sh pass the expected argv[0] basename to record-job. Replace `tr … | head -n 1` with `IFS= read -r -d '' arg0 < /proc/$p/cmdline` (one builtin, no pipe). Verify both launch branches in run-ablation.sh exec an external program and add a BSV case for an exec-ing non-setsid wrapper.
findings.failure_scenario: Failure: when the group leader's cmdline changes after record-job settled (or never diverges from the caller's), then on reclaim the live group is logged as stale/legacy, its record is removed and it is never TERM/KILLed, leaving the trial's client processes running after the batch is resumed.

findings.cross_file_justification: cmd_record_job (batch-supervisor.sh line 644) dies when <name> is outside ^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$ or on any usage error; run-ablation.sh's `|| printf … > .pgid` fallback (lines 1671, 1764) then writes a record with no .ident, which the new reclaim classifies as legacy and never signals.
findings.description: The fallback turns every record-job failure into a pre-cycle-134-style record. Under the new reclaim that record is 'legacy: never signalled, removed', so a live group is silently excluded from reclaim; the only diagnostic is a `die` line appended to the trial log and one WARN at reclaim time. If `jid` can contain any character outside the regex (`:`, `+`, `@`, `=` …) this applies to every job of the batch, which is a regression from the base where the group was killed. I could not verify the jid charset from the diff. Confidence: low-medium.
findings.failure_mode: Failure: when record-job exits non-zero for a reason other than a dead leader (name regex, usage, unwritable .ident), then the fallback .pgid is written for a live group and reclaim treats it as legacy, so the group survives every resume and the operator sees only a one-line WARN.
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop the fallback (a record-job failure should surface in the runner log and the trial should be treated as unreclaimable explicitly), or make it loud: log `jid=$jid record-job failed: group $pid will not be reclaimed` to the batch log, and add an assertion/test that every jid the runner generates matches the record-job name regex (or relax the regex to the filename-safe set the runner already relies on).
findings.failure_scenario: Failure: when record-job exits non-zero for a reason other than a dead leader (name regex, usage, unwritable .ident), then the fallback .pgid is written for a live group and reclaim treats it as legacy, so the group survives every resume and the operator sees only a one-line WARN.

findings.description: Both new error paths dereference `fp.stderr` as a str (`fp.stderr.strip()[:300]` at line 542, `fp.stderr.strip().splitlines()[-1][:200]` at line 601). That is correct only if the `g()` helper runs git with stderr captured in text mode. If `g()` lets stderr pass through (common in scripts that want git's own messages visible), `fp.stderr` is None and these lines raise AttributeError, replacing the intended `fail` (exit 1) / `refuse` (exit 2) with a traceback and Python's exit 1, which breaks the exit-code contract D-2.4 relies on. The helper is outside the diff so I could not confirm. Confidence: low.
findings.failure_mode: Failure: when the bounded fetch or the fix diff fails and g() does not capture stderr, then the handler itself crashes with AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'strip', the refusal message is never printed and the exit code is 1 instead of the documented 2.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm g() uses capture_output=True, text=True (or stderr=PIPE); otherwise guard with `(fp.stderr or '').strip()` in both places. SX-21…24 should assert the exit code and the message text for the diff-refusal path.
